headline: High-risk shared filesystem and MCP pathways create prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict exposure between ctx and Semantic Kernel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code events and uses MCP/stdio plus filesystem surfaces, while Semantic Kernel can use MCP servers and application-defined files. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if ctx outputs are consumed by SK without provenance checks. The interaction is documented enough to rate medium, not none.
conditions: IF ctx outputs are routed into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugins without provenance filtering
IF a shared MCP server or shared filesystem is used as the bridge between the agents
mitigations: Add provenance tags to ctx outputs before SK ingests them
Restrict SK plugins to allowlisted sources only
Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from files
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping middleware

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, and filesystem content; Semantic Kernel reads and writes filesystem data and can call external model APIs. If they share a workspace, ctx material can flow into SK and then to third-party inference backends. The profiles support this pathway, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF ctx and Semantic Kernel share the same filesystem or application workspace
IF SK forwards file contents or context to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, or Hugging Face APIs
mitigations: Move sensitive ctx artifacts to a separate directory
Turn off automatic file attachment in SK workflows
Use distinct API keys per agent
Redact logs before SK reads them
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can install packages and write files through filesystem surfaces, while Semantic Kernel can write the filesystem and use MCP. Both support multiple instances, and SK has no self-isolation. Concurrent writes to shared state can corrupt files or plugin state; uncertainty is limited, so high fits the default danger.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or shared plugin state
IF multiple instances run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate workspace
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable package installation in shared environments
Use per-instance plugin state directories
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx can emit observations from hooks and logs, and Semantic Kernel is a function-calling orchestration layer that may treat upstream context as authoritative. If SK consumes ctx output without verification, errors can cascade into downstream tool calls. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default agent workflows, but not proven high-impact here.
conditions: IF SK uses ctx-generated notes or logs as authoritative input
IF downstream plugins act on those inputs without a verification step
mitigations: Require human review before action-taking plugins run
Add a verification step between ctx and SK
Mark ctx outputs as untrusted metadata
Limit SK to read-only actions during testing
requires-engineering: implement source-of-truth checksums

E_compliance.rationale: ctx explicitly touches audit/runtime logs and harness records, while Semantic Kernel handles model provider API keys and plugin credentials and can send data to external model APIs. That creates a retention and disclosure mismatch risk if regulated data enters the shared workflow. The profiles do not show a specific residency breach, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in ctx logs or harness records
IF Semantic Kernel forwards that data to external model providers without a DPA or retention controls
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from ctx logs
Use a provider with an approved DPA
Set short retention on SK traces
Separate secrets from general context
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
